subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

items.prompt:
Homeostasis is
A) maintaining stable internal conditions
B) a type of cell
C) a kind of DNA
D) a bone

When you get too hot, your body
A) shivers
B) sweats to cool down
C) stops working
D) grows fur

steps: Sweating cools the body back to normal.

items.prompt:
When you get too cold, your body
A) sweats
B) shivers to warm up
C) melts
D) sleeps

steps: Shivering generates heat to warm up.

items.prompt:
After a meal, blood sugar rises and the body releases insulin to
A) raise it more
B) lower it back to normal
C) remove all sugar forever
D) do nothing
items.answer: B) lower it back to normal

steps: Insulin returns blood sugar to the set point.

items.prompt:
In negative feedback, a change away from normal triggers a response that
A) reverses it toward normal
B) makes it bigger
C) ignores it
D) deletes the cell

steps: Negative feedback returns a condition to its set point.

items.prompt:
Which is an internal condition the body keeps stable?
A) Body temperature
B) The weather outside
C) The time of day
D) The room color

steps: Temperature is kept stable by homeostasis.

items.prompt:
The best evidence that feedback controls body temperature is that after exercise it
A) keeps rising forever
B) rises then returns toward normal during rest
C) drops to zero
D) never changes
items.answer: B) rises then returns toward normal during rest

steps: Returning to normal shows feedback maintains homeostasis.

items.prompt:
Negative feedback keeps temperature near normal because
A) a rise triggers cooling and a fall triggers warming
B) it only heats
C) it only cools
D) it does nothing
items.answer: A) a rise triggers cooling and a fall triggers warming

steps: Opposite responses push temperature back to the set point.
